title: Add saturation dashboards + alert rules (queue depth, GPU pressure, throttling) aligned with saturation standard
author: Caleb Johnson
description: Context: This adds the first pass of standardized saturation dashboards + alert rules needed for the incident bot “saturation collector” (ENG-2844) and the broader saturation metrics audit/rollout (ENG-2848). Dashboards and alerts follow the definitions/label guidance in the saturation signals standard (Confluence: Observability Standards > Saturation Signals). Scope: (1) New “Saturation Overview” dashboard (service/region/model route pivots) that surfaces queueing + throttling + GPU pressure, with above-the-fold panels tuned for first 2–5 minutes of incident triage; (2) New drilldown dashboard “Saturation: GPU + Scheduler” with SM occupancy vs util, scheduler contention, KV cache pressure proxies, and batching/backpressure indicators; (3) Alert rules for queue depth, sustained throttling, and scheduler contention with guardrails to avoid paging on raw utilization; (4) Annotation lanes for deploy/config change overlays (expects the new annotation event stream; panels render even if annotations are missing). Notes/assumptions: These alerts are intentionally conservative to reduce noise during initial rollout; thresholds are set to catch sustained saturation rather than transient bursts. We explicitly avoid “GPU util > X” style paging and instead alert on queue depth + throttling + scheduler contention combinations. All rules are scoped to prod clusters and require region label presence; if labels are missing, the series is excluded (prevents accidental high-cardinality + avoids misleading partial data). Rollout: dashboards ship immediately; alerts are created in disabled state by default and enabled per-region after label validation (ENG-2848 checklist). Testing: validated panels against last 7 days in us-east + eu-west; spot-checked against SUP-4933 symptoms (throttling/429s) and internal synthetic saturation tests. Follow-ups: (a) After rollout, revisit queue depth thresholds for smaller regions; (b) add per-model route “top N offenders” table once label normalization from PR-18460 is fully deployed; (c) tune alerts for Dedicated pools separately (different SLOs and traffic patterns).
commits: dashboards: add saturation_overview.jsonnet with queue depth + throttling + GPU pressure panels
alerts: add saturation_alerts.libsonnet (queue depth sustained, throttling sustained, scheduler contention)
metrics: add recording rules for normalized queue depth and throttling ratios
dashboards: add saturation_gpu_scheduler_drilldown.jsonnet (SM occupancy, scheduler contention, KV cache pressure proxies)
docs: add runbook links + panel descriptions + expected labels
chore: wire dashboards into pack index + CI validation
ci_checks: policy check (prod scoping + label allowlist) — pass
conversation: Allison Grant (review): The dashboards look good, but we should not page on GPU utilization/occupancy alone. Can we ensure every paging rule includes either queue depth or throttling or scheduler contention? Also, please add a short doc snippet clarifying why SM occupancy is shown even though it’s not directly paged on.

Caleb Johnson (author): Updated rules to remove the standalone SM occupancy condition and require (queue_depth_sustained OR throttling_ratio_sustained) plus scheduler contention as a secondary signal. Added docs section “Why SM occupancy is in the dashboard but not an alert trigger.”

Logan Wright (review): Thresholds: queue_depth > 200 for 10m feels high for small regions but might be OK for us-east. Can we make the alert relative (e.g., p95 queue depth / capacity) or at least gate it on sustained throttling? Also please scope alerts to prod only; I see a couple queries missing env=prod.

Caleb Johnson (author): Added env=prod scoping across all rules. For now, gated the queue depth page on sustained throttling OR scheduler contention for 10m to reduce false positives in small regions. I left a TODO to move to capacity-relative thresholds once the capacity metric is reliable across clusters (tracked in ENG-2848).

Miles Thornton (review): Region-awareness: can we ensure region label is required? If missing, the aggregation will hide multi-region splits and mislead responders. Also watch cardinality on model_route.

Caleb Johnson (author): Enforced region label via explicit matchers and excluded missing-label series. For model_route, overview defaults to service+region; model_route is only used in drilldowns and is filtered + top-k in the table panel. Also added a note about cardinality guardrails and pointed to the normalization work in the platform repo.

Rafael Mendes (review): Please add runbook links directly on the “throttling sustained” panel and include a hint that the incident bot saturation collector will link here. Also: alert labels should include a stable routing/service identifier responders recognize.

Caleb Johnson (author): Added runbook links and a panel description targeted at incident responders (first 2–5 min triage). Updated alert labels/annotations to include service, region, and route (when present) using the standardized label keys used by the incident bot collector.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved after changes. Conservative thresholds + gating on throttling/scheduler contention are the right call for initial rollout; we can tune after two weeks of data.
Logan Wright (approval): LGTM. Please keep the follow-up item for capacity-relative queue depth; that’s the long-term fix.
release_notes:
- New saturation dashboards: overview + GPU/scheduler drilldown (queue depth, throttling, GPU pressure, scheduler contention)
- New conservative alert rules aligned with saturation signals standard; enabled per-region after label validation
- Documentation added for responders and for incident bot collector linking
